title: Cycle Pulse Bands: time-boxed staffing bands and priority-curvature framework for scope curation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: recurring mid-cycle scope drift and uneven staffing lead to overruns and rushed scope cuts. Goal: introduce a lightweight operational layer — 'Cycle Pulse Bands' — that pairs time-boxed staffing bands with a reproducible priority-curvature scoring matrix to make capacity tradeoffs deterministic, auditable, and easy to communicate across PM/Eng/Design. The output is a prescriptive weekly staffing ledger, a small surge credit pool, and a decision rubric for scope trims that preserves OKR impact while minimizing engineering churn.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pilot runs for 2026-W12 with at least two cross-functional initiatives using Pulse Bands and a completed post-mortem
2) Staffing ledger auto-generated each Monday with band assignments and estimated FTE fractions for the week
3) Priority-curvature rubric published and applied to all candidate scope trims with owner signoff
4) Surge credit pool defined (0.5-1.0 FTE-week equivalent) and mechanism for drawdown/repay documented
5) Tooling prototype (spreadsheet + small script) to score tickets available in the shared drive and used by pilot teams
notes: Trade-offs: lightweight process favored over heavy gating. Aim is deterministic behavior, not bureaucratic approval flows.
We prioritize reproducibility: scoring inputs must be simple (OKR impact, customer urgency, engineering effort, regression risk).
Risk: teams may treat Pulse Bands as a hard cap; communications plan needed to position it as a flexible guardrail.
Pilot scope limited to Platform and Console squads to validate cross-team constraints and runtime-induced dependencies.
